summary: Amrith Krishna works in linguistics and Indology. He has held posts at Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur, University of Cambridge, IT University of Copenhagen, Oriflow, Uniphore (attested 2023), and Learno.AI (attested 2024–2025).

Amy Heller, a Tibetologist and historian-archaeologist, earned degrees from Barnard College, INALCO, and the EPHE under Ariane Macdonald. She has held posts at Yale, CNRS, Sapienza University of Rome, Sichuan University, SOAS, INALCO, and the University of Bern.

Amy Paris Langenberg is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. She earned her PhD from Columbia University around 2001–2008 and became an assistant professor of religious studies at Eckerd College around 2014.

Amy Sims Miller specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her BA at Wesleyan University and an MA and PhD at the University of Virginia under David Germano, alongside studies with various traditional and academic teachers.

Amy Snyder Ohta is a scholar in linguistics and Japanology. She studied at the University of California, Los Angeles in 1990 and 1993, and became a professor at the University of Washington around 1995.

Ana Agud is a linguist and Indologist. She studied at the University of Salamanca (1965–1970) and the University of Tübingen (1970–1974) before becoming a professor in classical and Indo-European philology at Salamanca around 1976.

Anagarika Dharmapala was a Buddhist studies and religious studies figure who studied at institutions including S. Thomas' College and Royal College, Colombo. He founded the Maha Bodhi Society in 1891 as well as the Maha Bodhi Society of India.

Anagarika Govinda worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. Educated at Freiburg, Naples, and Cagliari, he studied under Nyanatiloka and Tomo Geshe Rinpoche, taught at Indian universities including Visva-Bharati and Patna, and led the Arya Maitreya Mandala.

Anagarika Munindra was a Buddhist and religious studies teacher. He served as superintendent of the Mahabodhi Temple from 1953 to 1957 and studied under Mahasi Sayadaw (1957–1966) and Satya Narayan Goenka.

Anam Thubten Rinpoche works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teacher Tsurlo Rinpoche and has served as a teacher at the Vajrayana Foundation College of Buddhist Studies.

Anand A. Yang is a historian and Indologist. He studied at Swarthmore College and the University of Virginia, holding posts at Sweet Briar College, the University of Utah, and the University of Washington (around 2002).

Anand Venkatkrishnan specializes in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He completed his doctoral thesis at Columbia University in 2015 and serves as an assistant professor at the University of Chicago (attested 2026).

Ananda Guruge was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. Educated at the University of Ceylon and the University of London, he held posts at NIEPA, California State University, Fullerton, and the University of the West.

Ananda Kentish Coomaraswamy worked in Indology, history-archaeology, and philosophy. Educated at Wycliffe College, UCL, and under Caroline Rhys Davids, he directed the Geological Survey of Ceylon and served as curator and research fellow at Boston's Museum of Fine Arts.

Anant Sadashiv Altekar was an Indologist and historian-archaeologist. He served as professor and department head at Banaras Hindu University (1930–1952), university professor at Patna University (1952–1959), and director of the K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute (1955).

Anantalal Thakur was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at the University of Calcutta and with several traditional teachers. He held professorships at the Mithila Institute (1952–1969) and directed the K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute (1968–1971).

Anantanand Rambachan is a scholar of religious studies, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at the University of the West Indies, University of Leeds, and under Dayananda Saraswati, and served as professor of religion at St. Olaf College (1985–2021).

Andrea Acri is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He completed his PhD at Leiden University under Arlo Griffiths and Willem van der Molen, and was appointed maître de conférences in tantric studies at EPHE in 2016.

Andrea R. Jain is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who studied at Southern Methodist University and Rice University (PhD 2010). She has taught at IUPUI and advanced from assistant to full professor at Indiana University Bloomington (2010–2021).

Andrea Schlosser is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who earned her master's and PhD at the Free University of Berlin. As of 2026, she is affiliated with the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities and the University of Munich.
